title.rendered: AP Exam Dates 2026: Full Schedule & Key Deadlines

content.rendered:
Key Summary

  • Two Exam Weeks In May: The 2026 AP exams run across two weeks, May 4 to May 8 and May 11 to May 15, with morning and afternoon sessions each day.
  • Late Testing Window: Students with an approved conflict can sit alternate exams during the late-testing period, May 18 to May 22, 2026.
  • Portfolio Deadlines Come First: AP Seminar, Research and Computer Science Principles work is due April 30, and AP Art and Design portfolios are due May 8, 2026.
  • Scores Release In July: 2026 AP scores become available from Monday, July 6, released in waves by region, with international students typically later in the rollout.
  • Local Time Applies Everywhere: Exams start at 8 a.m. and 12 p.m. local time, so UAE students test on the same calendar dates as the rest of the world, just on Gulf time.

AP planning rarely goes wrong because a student did not study. It goes wrong because someone misread the schedule, missed a portfolio deadline, or assumed exam dates were flexible when they are not. Parents in particular tell us they just want one reliable, current source that lays out exactly when everything happens, without digging through five different pages. 

This guide does that, with every date checked against the College Board, and written for students and parents in the UAE rather than a generic US audience. You will get the full 2026 AP exam schedule, subject by subject, the late-testing window, registration and portfolio deadlines, when scores are released, and what the timing actually means if you are sitting these exams from Dubai or elsewhere in the UAE. Ignite Training Institute’s AP tutoring work is built around exactly this kind of schedule-aligned planning, so the advice here is practical, not theoretical.

What Are The AP Exam Dates For 2026?

The first thing most students search for is simple: when is my exam? The 2026 AP exams take place over two weeks in May, from May 4 to May 8 and from May 11 to May 15, 2026. Each subject has its own fixed date and session. Late testing runs from May 18 to May 22 for approved students. The dates are set by the College Board and are the same worldwide, including across the UAE.

AP exams are not flexible. Every subject is assigned a specific day and a specific session, and you sit for it then. This is different from many other qualifications students in the UAE take, so it is worth understanding early. There is no option to pick a more convenient slot, and early testing is not permitted under any circumstances.

AP Exam Start Times

Every AP exam begins at one of two times, based on your school’s local time:

  • Morning exams begin between 8 and 9 am. local time
  • Afternoon exams begin between 12 and 1 pm. local time

For a student in the UAE, that means Gulf Standard Time. Your school’s AP coordinator confirms the exact reporting time and room, so the session times below tell you which half of the day your exam falls in, not the precise minute you walk in.

Know More About: How Long Are AP Exams? Subject-Wise Breakdown

2026 AP Exam Schedule: Full Subject-By-Subject Dates

This is the part most students actually need: find your subject, find your date. The schedule below is the official College Board 2026 administration. Week 1 covers May 4 to May 8, and Week 2 covers May 11 to May 15. Morning means the 8 a.m. local session, and afternoon means the 12 p.m. local session.

Week 1: May 4 To May 8, 2026

Week 2: May 11 To May 15, 2026

One thing to check early: if two of your subjects share the same date and session, that is a conflict you cannot solve yourself. Your AP coordinator orders a late-testing exam for one of them, which is why the next section matters even for students who plan to test in the main window. For the full picture of what each course involves, the official subject list is a useful companion to this schedule.

AP Digital Portfolio Submission Deadlines

A few subjects are not decided by a single exam day. Their work is submitted online before testing week, and missing these deadlines is one of the most common avoidable mistakes:

  • AP Seminar and AP Research: April 30, 2026 (11:59 pm. ET) to submit performance tasks as final
  • AP Computer Science Principles: April 30, 2026 (11:59 pm. ET) to submit the Create performance task as final
  • AP Art and Design: May 8, 2026 (8 pm. ET) to submit all three portfolio components as final

Note that these deadlines are in US Eastern Time. For a UAE student, ET is eight hours behind Gulf Standard Time, so an 11:59 p.m. ET deadline on April 30 is early morning on May 1 in Dubai. Plan submissions a clear day ahead rather than against the local-time wire.

Know More About: AP Courses & Exams: Complete List For High Schoolers

AP Late-Testing Dates 2026 (May 18 To May 22)

Late testing exists for students who genuinely cannot sit an exam in the main two weeks. It is not a way to buy more revision time, and you cannot request it yourself. The decision sits with your school.

Who Qualifies For Late Testing?

Late testing is approved for specific situations, not preference. Common valid reasons include illness on exam day, a documented emergency, two exams scheduled in the same session, or certain approved scheduling conflicts such as a clashing school commitment.

Your AP coordinator confirms eligibility and orders the alternate exam through the College Board. Late-testing exams are different versions of the paper, designed to be comparable in difficulty, so there is no advantage or disadvantage built into taking one.

The Late-Testing Schedule

The 2026 late-testing window runs from Monday, May 18 to Friday, May 22, 2026. The same local-time rule applies, with morning sessions starting between 8 and 9 a.m. and afternoon sessions between 12 and 1 p.m.

Specific subjects are grouped onto specific late-testing days, so if you are approved, your coordinator will tell you exactly which day and session your alternate exam falls on. Do not assume a late seat is available until your school confirms it. The full official late-testing schedule is below.

Know More About: How To Register For AP Exams 2026? Process & Deadline

AP Exam Registration Deadlines And Key Dates To Know

The exam dates are only half the timeline. The deadlines that decide whether you can sit an exam at all happen months earlier, and they are where students in international schools most often slip.

When AP Registration Closes?

Most schools close standard AP registration in the autumn of the previous year, typically around November 2025 for May 2026 exams. A late-registration period, usually carrying an additional fee, generally extends into March 2026. Exact cut-offs are set by your school, not just the College Board, because your school coordinates ordering.

The practical takeaway: if a student decides in February that they want to add an AP exam, that may already be a late registration, and after the late window, it is usually not possible at all. The full process and fee detail is worth reading early, well before the deadline pressure starts. You can see the steps in How To Register For AP Exams 2026? Process & Deadline.

The Full 2026 AP Timeline At A Glance

Putting the whole year in order makes the pressure points obvious:

  • Autumn 2025: standard AP registration closes at most schools
  • Into March 2026: late registration window, usually with a fee
  • April 30, 2026: AP Seminar, Research and Computer Science Principles digital submissions due
  • May 4 to May 15, 2026: main AP exam administration
  • May 8, 2026: AP Art and Design portfolio components due
  • May 18 to May 22, 2026: late-testing window
  • July 6, 2026: AP scores begin to be released

Know More About: All About AP Exams 2025 Explained: A Detailed Overview

When Are AP Scores Released In 2026?

After the exam, the next question is always the same: when do scores come out? For 2026, the answer is clear.

The July 6, 2026 Release

2026 AP scores become available starting Monday, July 6, 2026, through your College Board account. Scores are not all released at once. The College Board rolls them out in waves by region to manage demand, with releases typically beginning around 8 a.m. US Eastern Time on the release day.

Some scores, particularly from late testing or exams with administrative complications, can take longer. If a score has not appeared by August 15, that is the point at which the College Board recommends contacting AP Services for Students.

What International Students Should Expect?

Students outside the United States, including those in the UAE, are generally later in the rolling release than US East Coast students. If your score is not visible the moment release day begins, that is normal and not a problem with your result.

Use the same College Board account you registered with, avoid creating a second account, and make sure the email on the account is current well before July. For what the 1 to 5 scale means and how colleges use it, our dedicated scores guide goes into the detail this section deliberately keeps short.

Know More About: AP Scores: Everything You Need To Know

Taking AP Exams In The UAE: Local Timing And Logistics

Most AP date guides are written as though every reader is in an American time zone. Students in Dubai and across the UAE sit the same exams on the same calendar dates, but a few practical details are worth getting right.

What “8 a.m. Local Time” Means For UAE Students

The College Board sets sessions by local time, so a UAE student’s morning exam starts in the 8 to 9 a.m. Gulf Standard Time window, and the afternoon session in the 12 to 1 p.m. window. You do not convert from US time.

The only place time zones matter is for ET deadlines, such as the digital portfolio submissions, where Gulf Standard Time runs eight hours ahead of US Eastern Time. That gap works in your favour for deadlines if you submit a day early, and against you if you leave it to the final hours.

AP Test Centres And Digital Testing In The UAE

AP exams in the UAE are administered through schools and authorised test centres rather than being booked individually like some other international tests. If a student’s own school does not offer a particular AP subject, they usually need to arrange to sit it at a school or centre that does, and that arrangement has to be made well before registration closes, not in exam season.

Many AP exams are now delivered digitally through the College Board’s Bluebook application, so part of preparing is making sure the student is comfortable with the digital format and has practised in it, not just with past paper content.

Planning Your Revision Backwards From The Exam Date

The most useful thing the schedule gives you is a fixed endpoint to plan against. A practical approach is to work backwards: identify your exam date, then set your structured revision to peak in the two weeks before it, with full timed practice in the final fortnight rather than the first content review.

For a student sitting, say, Biology on May 4, serious structured revision should be well underway by March, not starting after the Easter break. Spreading subjects out using their actual dates, rather than treating “May” as one block, is what prevents the last-week pile-up most students fall into.

Know More About: 10 Proven Tips On How To Study For AP Exams & Score Well

Ignite’s AP Tutors In Dubai, Helping You Plan Around The Exams

Knowing the dates is the easy part. Turning them into a realistic preparation plan, across several AP subjects with overlapping deadlines, is where most students need structure. Ignite works with AP students across Dubai and the UAE to build study plans anchored to the actual exam calendar, not a vague sense of “May”.

Our approach is practical and schedule-led. Students get personalised tutoring matched to their subjects, timed past-paper and digital practice ahead of the relevant exam date, and experienced AP tutors who know where students lose marks under time pressure. The aim is steady readiness by exam week rather than a last-minute scramble. 

Families looking for AP tutors in Dubai can build a plan around the exact dates that matter for their subjects, and our guidance on how to study for AP exams is a useful starting point.

Know More About: 2026 AP Exams Guide: All You Need To Know

FAQs

1. When Do AP Exams Start And End In 2026?

The 2026 AP exams start on Monday, May 4, 2026 and the main administration ends on Friday, May 15, 2026. Testing runs across two weeks, May 4 to May 8 and May 11 to May 15, with a separate late-testing window from May 18 to May 22 for approved students.

2. Do AP Exam Dates Change Every Year?

Yes, the specific dates shift each year, but the pattern is consistent. AP exams are almost always held over the first two full weeks of May, with morning and afternoon sessions and a late-testing window the following week.

The subjects and their order can move slightly year to year, so always confirm against the current year’s schedule rather than relying on last year’s dates.

3. What Time Do AP Exams Start?

AP exams begin between 8 and 9 a.m. local time for morning sessions and between 12 and 1 p.m. local time for afternoon sessions. For UAE students this means Gulf Standard Time. Your AP coordinator confirms the exact reporting time and location.

4. When is AP Late Testing In 2026?

The 2026 AP late-testing window runs from Monday, May 18 to Friday, May 22, 2026. Late testing is only for students with an approved reason, such as illness, an emergency, or two exams scheduled at the same time. Students cannot request late testing themselves; the school arranges it.

5. Can You Take Two AP Exams On The Same Day?

You can take a morning exam and an afternoon exam on the same day. If two of your subjects are scheduled in the same session, that is a conflict, and your AP coordinator will arrange for one of them to be taken during the late-testing window.

6. When Are AP Exam Dates Released Each Year?

The College Board usually publishes the next year’s AP exam dates well in advance, generally in the year before the exams. This gives schools and students time to plan registration, coursework and revision around a confirmed schedule.

7. When Will 2026 AP Scores Be Released?

2026 AP scores become available starting Monday, July 6, 2026, through your College Board account. Scores are released in waves by region, and international students, including those in the UAE, are typically later in the rollout. If a score has not appeared by August 15, contact AP Services for Students.

8. Are AP Exam Dates The Same Worldwide, Including The UAE?

Yes. The College Board sets one global schedule, and exams are sat on the same calendar dates everywhere, including across the UAE. The only difference is that start times follow local time, so a UAE student tests on Gulf Standard Time on the same day as a student in the US.

Know More About:  How Long Are AP Exams? Subject-Wise Breakdown

Conclusion

The 2026 AP exams come down to a few fixed points: two exam weeks from May 4 to May 15, a late-testing window from May 18 to May 22, portfolio deadlines at the end of April and on May 8, and scores from July 6. Get those into your calendar early, check whether any of your subjects clash, and treat the registration deadline in the previous autumn as the real starting line.

The students who handle AP well are not the ones who study hardest in the final week. They are the ones who planned backwards from these dates months earlier.

If you want help turning the schedule into a subject-by-subject plan, speak with our academic team or book a free demo class, and we will map it out with you.
